sections.h2: Where in Warrenton is the deeds counter?
sections.html:
The counter is on South Main Street at number 109. The register's site lists Monday to Friday service from 8:30 to 5, a phone at (252) 257-3265, and a post office box, number 506, with the 27589 ZIP. The job is filled at the ballot box every second year, per G.S. 161-1 provides.

Warren County was created in 1779 and carries the name of a doctor who died at Bunker Hill, the county manager's page explains. Some 20,000 people share its 443 square miles of fields, and five commissioners hold the board seats. One counter covers all of it, so a quick call can save a drive.

Anyone may read what the office holds. Lookups run on names, so a person hunting for a parcel's owner should have one; with only a street address, the FAQ redirects to the tax office at (252) 257-4158.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Warren County accomplish?
sections.html:
Recording shields the buyer. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded transfer, or a lease longer than three years, cannot beat a lien creditor or a paying purchaser. Whoever registers first stands first.

By its own account the office exists so owners can publish their interest in real estate. It also files births that happened in Warren County, marriage licenses and notary oaths, and it files DD-214 papers for retired service members at no cost.

  • The land side takes deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and powers of attorney.
  • Wills live elsewhere, with the courthouse clerk.
  • Liens and judgments: the FAQ gives the clerk's number, (252) 257-6300.

sections.h2: What does filing a Warren County deed cost?
sections.html:
Warren County follows G.S. 161-10. Twenty-six dollars buys the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed and every page after costs four. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages, with the same four-dollar overage. Filing a release costs nothing.

The county's own fee page and FAQ were written years ago and show other per-page and mortgage numbers than the statute does. Call before mailing a package, and use the statute figures as your starting point.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamp in Warren County?
sections.html:
Sellers pay. For each $500 of value, or any leftover part of $500, the stamp is one dollar, handed to the register before the deed is entered.

The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest travels to the state monthly, less a small allowance (statute). The old office FAQ restates the rate as $2 per $1,000. The settlement statement shows the exact stamp.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller line up first?
sections.html:
Three items come first: matching names, a current tax account and a document that fits the office's format. The register's website carries a recording checklist and a fee page, and staff answer by phone.

  • Changing who is named takes a fresh deed. The office recommends an attorney, then the normal filing fee, plus stamp tax where a price is involved.
  • Check the tax account. Each bill is due on September 1 and starts drawing interest after January 5, per G.S. 105-360.
  • Ask the clerk if a lien or judgment sits on the file.
  • Pay with cash, check or money order, since the FAQ rules out cards.

Two short calls, one to each office, before listing.

sections.h2: How does rural Warren County shape a sale?
sections.html:
Farm tracts and family land come up often in a county of this size, and such sales may add a survey, plat or easement, each filed separately. A plat is $21 a sheet by statute. Splitting acreage? Learn the register's plat format before the surveyor starts.

In the FAQ, a copy of a recorded map is five cents a page (fifty for large maps) and a deed copy is also five cents. The online search shows scanned deeds. Tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial photos come from tax mapping, not here.

Heirs who want to sell should see whether a deed was ever recorded in their names; estate papers may start at the clerk.

sections.h2: How far back do Warren County genealogy and vital records reach?
sections.html:
The county's genealogy page gives a short timeline for what the register keeps. Birth and death certificates run from 1914 to the present. Delayed birth certificates reach back to the late 1800s. Marriage indexes begin in 1867, and marriage bonds and licenses go back to the late 1800s.

  • Certificates, bonds and licenses are filed only for events that took place in Warren County.
  • NC Vital Records in Raleigh holds records for every county in the state and is the place to ask about events elsewhere.
  • Wills are not here. The page says the Warren County clerk of court maintains them.

Heirs selling a Warren County house will find the register useful for the marriage and death side of the family story, while the will itself sits with the clerk.

NC Vital Records lists its Raleigh phone line as 919.733.3526 on the county page. If an owner died in another county, the record will not be in Warren County's files, so ask the state office or the county where the death happened.

sections.h2: What non-land business does the Warren County office do?
sections.html:
Many visitors come for other reasons. A marriage license costs sixty dollars, lasts sixty days and is booked by phone. A certified marriage certificate is ten dollars and can be had once ten days have passed since the ceremony.

A certified vital record goes only to a short list: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, a legal representative, or someone with proof of a legal need. Plain copies are open to all.

New notaries swear in at the counter without an appointment, bringing the notice from the Secretary of State, for a $10 fee per the FAQ. Births outside the county are recorded by NC Vital Records.

sections.h2: Can a Warren County house with liens or repairs still sell?
sections.html:
Yes. Liens and back taxes come out of the price at closing and the releases get recorded. A tired house can find a buyer willing to take it as it stands.

Start the title work early so both the register's index and the clerk's judgments are checked. For a cash number on a Warren County house to set beside a listing, ask this site.

sections.h2: Where can a Warren County owner look up or pay a tax bill?
sections.html:
The county's property page for the register of deeds links to a combined tool for paying tax bills and searching property record cards. It is a county web page, so the register's staff still direct questions about assessments to the tax office at the number in the FAQ.

Keep the bill and the recorded deed together. When a closing is scheduled, the person handling it will want the account number and the book and page of the last recorded deed, and both come from those two lookups.

faqs.q: Is releasing a Warren County mortgage free?
faqs.a: Yes, no fee applies to recording a satisfaction of a mortgage or deed of trust, under the state schedule.

faqs.q: Can Warren County staff name a parcel's owner from an address?
faqs.a: No. Staff search by name only, so address-only callers are sent to the tax office.

faqs.q: Does the Warren County deeds office file wills?
faqs.a: No. The clerk of superior court takes wills and estates. The register takes deeds, mortgages, plats, releases, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

faqs.q: Does Warren County charge to record a DD-214?
faqs.a: No, the office files discharge papers for retired military free.

faqs.q: Who answers deed questions in Warren County?
faqs.a: Phone (252) 257-3265, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. The office is at 109 South Main Street, Warrenton.
